75:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Qiyamah In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful It has been mentioned more than once that if the thing sworn upon is not present, it is permissible to use la before the oath to confirm the negation. What is being sworn to here is the proof of the Resurrection and the refutation of what the ignorant among the servants claim about the non-resurrection of bodies. For this reason, God the Almighty said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection, nor do I swear by the self-reproaching soul. Al-Hasan said: He swore by the Day of Resurrection, not by the self-reproaching soul. Qatada said: Rather, He swore by both of them. This is how Ibn Abi Hatim related it. Ibn Jarir related on the authority of Al-Hasan and Al-A’raj that they both recited: I swear by the Day of Resurrection. This supports Al-Hasan’s statement because he affirmed the oath by the Day of Resurrection and denied the oath by the self-reproaching soul. The correct view is that He swore by both of them, as Qatada may God have mercy on him said. This is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Jarir chose it. As for the Day of Resurrection, it is well-known, and as for the self-reproaching soul, Qurra ibn Khalid said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding this verse: By God, we see the believer only blaming himself. I did not mean by my words, I did not mean by my food, I did not mean by my inner conversation. The wicked person continues without blaming himself. Juwaybir said: It has reached us on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said regarding his statement: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul, he said: There is no one among the people of the heavens and the earth who will not blame himself on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Saleh bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, that he asked Ikrimah about the statement of God, {And I swear by the self-reproaching soul}. He said: It blames itself for good and evil if it did such and such. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Waki’, on the authority of Isra’il, on its authority. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Mu’ammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding the statement of God, {And I swear by the self-reproaching soul}. He said: It blames itself for good and evil. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa’id that he asked Ibn Abbas about that, and he said: It is the self-reproaching soul. Ali bin Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid that it regrets what has passed and blames itself for it. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the self-reproaching, blameworthy soul. Qatadah said: The self-reproaching soul is the wicked one. Ibn Jarir said: All of these sayings are close in meaning, and what is most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation is that it is the one that blames its owner for good and evil and regrets what has passed. God the Almighty says: {Does man think that We will not assemble his bones} meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, does he think that We are not able to restore his bones and assemble them from their scattered places? {Yes, We are Able to put in perfect order his fingertips}. Sa`id ibn Jubayr and Al-`Awfi reported from Ibn `Abbas: that We make him hoofed or barefoot. This is what Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Jarir said. Ibn Jarir explained this by saying that if God had willed, He could have done that in this world. What is apparent from the verse is that His saying, {Able} is a condition of His saying, {Assemble}, meaning, does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Rather, We will assemble them, Able to put in perfect order his fingertips, meaning, Our ability is sufficient to assemble them. And if We willed, We could have resurrected him more than he was, and made his fingertips, which are the tips of his fingers, even. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Qutaybah and Az-Zajjaj. And His statement: Rather, man desires to explode before him, Saeed said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning to go forward. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: To explode before him means hope. Man says, I will work and then repent before the Day of Resurrection. It is said: It refers to disbelief in the truth before the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: To explode before him means to go ahead riding his head. Al-Hasan said: No son of Adam will be encountered except that his soul is drawn to disobeying God step by step, except for the one whom God protects. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and more than one of the early Muslims: He is the one who hastens to commit sins and delays repentance. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is the disbeliever who denies the Day of Reckoning. Ibn Zayd said the same, and this is what is most apparent of what is meant. That is why He said after it: He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?' That is, he says, When will the Day of Resurrection be? His question is a question of improbability of its occurrence and a denial of its existence, as God the Almighty said: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you should be truthful?' Say, 'You have an appointment for a Day from which you will not delay an hour, nor will you advance it.' And God the Almighty said here: {And when the sight is dazed} Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ read it with a kasra on the ra’, meaning dazzled. What he said is similar to the statement of God the Almighty: {Their glances will not return to them}, meaning they will look in terror like this and that, their sight not settling on anything due to the intensity of the terror. Others read it with a fatha, which is close in meaning to the first. The point is that the eyes will be dazzled on the Day of Resurrection and will be humbled, bewildered, and humiliated by the intensity of the horrors and the enormity of what they will witness on the Day of Resurrection of matters. And the statement of God the Almighty: {And the moon will be eclipsed}, meaning its light will be gone. And the sun and the moon will be joined together Mujahid said: coiled. Ibn Zayd read when explaining this verse: {When the sun is wrapped up * And when the stars are extinguished}. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read: And the sun and the moon will be joined together. God the Almighty says: On that Day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’ That is, when the son of Adam witnesses these horrors on the Day of Resurrection, he will want to flee and will say, Where is the escape? That is, is there a refuge or a place of refuge? God the Almighty says: No! No burden! To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and more than one of the early Muslims said: That is, there is no escape. This verse is like God the Almighty’s saying: For you there is no refuge that Day, nor will you be denied. That is, you will have no place to flee in. Likewise, He said here: No burden, that is, you will have no place to seek refuge in. That is why He said: To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement, that is, the return and destination. Then God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind meaning he will be informed of all his deeds, old and new, first and last, small and great, as God the Almighty said: “And they will find present what they did. And your Lord does not wrong anyone” and likewise He said here: Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses meaning he is a witness against himself and knows what he did, even if he apologizes and denies it. And as God the Almighty said: “Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rather, man is a witness against himself meaning: his hearing, sight, hands, feet and limbs. Qatada said: He is a witness against himself. In another narration he said: If you wish, by God you will see him seeing the faults and sins of people, yet heedless of his own. And it was said: It is written in the Gospel: O son of Adam, you see the speck in your brother’s eye and leave the log in your own eye and do not see it! Mujahid said: Even if he presents his excuses and even if he argues about them, then he is aware of them. Qatadah said: Even if he presents his excuses and even if he apologizes on that day with a false excuse, it will not be accepted from him. As-Suddi said: Even if he presents his excuses is his proof. Ibn Zayd, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said the same, and Ibn Jarir preferred it. Qatadah said on the authority of Zurarah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Even if he presents his excuses means: If he throws down his clothes. Ad-Dahhak said: Even if he throws down his curtain. The people of Yemen call the curtain an excuse. The correct statement is the statement of Mujahid and his companions, like the statement of God the Almighty: {The Day God will resurrect them all, then they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.} Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {Even if he presents his excuses} is an apology. Have you not heard that He said: Their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers and that He said: “And they will offer to God that Day peace” {So they will offer peace: We had not done any evil} and their statement: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists}.

He said: It blames itself for good and evil. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa’id that he asked Ibn Abbas about that, and he said: It is the self-reproaching soul. Ali bin Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid that it regrets what has passed and blames itself for it. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the self-reproaching, blameworthy soul. Qatadah said: The self-reproaching soul is the wicked one. Ibn Jarir said: All of these sayings are close in meaning, and what is most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation is that it is the one that blames its owner for good and evil and regrets what has passed. God the Almighty says: {Does man think that We will not assemble his bones} meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, does he think that We are not able to restore his bones and assemble them from their scattered places? {Yes, We are Able to put in perfect order his fingertips}. Sa`id ibn Jubayr and Al-`Awfi reported from Ibn `Abbas: that We make him hoofed or barefoot. This is what Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Jarir said. Ibn Jarir explained this by saying that if God had willed, He could have done that in this world. What is apparent from the verse is that His saying, {Able} is a condition of His saying, {Assemble}, meaning, does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Rather, We will assemble them, Able to put in perfect order his fingertips, meaning, Our ability is sufficient to assemble them. And if We willed, We could have resurrected him more than he was, and made his fingertips, which are the tips of his fingers, even. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Qutaybah and Az-Zajjaj. And His statement: Rather, man desires to explode before him, Saeed said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning to go forward. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: To explode before him means hope. Man says, I will work and then repent before the Day of Resurrection. It is said: It refers to disbelief in the truth before the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: To explode before him means to go ahead riding his head. Al-Hasan said: No son of Adam will be encountered except that his soul is drawn to disobeying God step by step, except for the one whom God protects. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and more than one of the early Muslims: He is the one who hastens to commit sins and delays repentance. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is the disbeliever who denies the Day of Reckoning. Ibn Zayd said the same, and this is what is most apparent of what is meant. That is why He said after it: He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?' That is, he says, When will the Day of Resurrection be? His question is a question of improbability of its occurrence and a denial of its existence, as God the Almighty said: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you should be truthful?' Say, 'You have an appointment for a Day from which you will not delay an hour, nor will you advance it.' And God the Almighty said here: {And when the sight is dazed} Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ read it with a kasra on the ra’, meaning dazzled. What he said is similar to the statement of God the Almighty: {Their glances will not return to them}, meaning they will look in terror like this and that, their sight not settling on anything due to the intensity of the terror. Others read it with a fatha, which is close in meaning to the first. The point is that the eyes will be dazzled on the Day of Resurrection and will be humbled, bewildered, and humiliated by the intensity of the horrors and the enormity of what they will witness on the Day of Resurrection of matters. And the statement of God the Almighty: {And the moon will be eclipsed}, meaning its light will be gone. And the sun and the moon will be joined together Mujahid said: coiled. Ibn Zayd read when explaining this verse: {When the sun is wrapped up * And when the stars are extinguished}. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read: And the sun and the moon will be joined together. God the Almighty says: On that Day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’ That is, when the son of Adam witnesses these horrors on the Day of Resurrection, he will want to flee and will say, Where is the escape? That is, is there a refuge or a place of refuge? God the Almighty says: No! No burden! To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and more than one of the early Muslims said: That is, there is no escape. This verse is like God the Almighty’s saying: For you there is no refuge that Day, nor will you be denied. That is, you will have no place to flee in. Likewise, He said here: No burden, that is, you will have no place to seek refuge in. That is why He said: To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement, that is, the return and destination. Then God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind meaning he will be informed of all his deeds, old and new, first and last, small and great, as God the Almighty said: “And they will find present what they did. And your Lord does not wrong anyone” and likewise He said here: Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses meaning he is a witness against himself and knows what he did, even if he apologizes and denies it. And as God the Almighty said: “Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rather, man is a witness against himself meaning: his hearing, sight, hands, feet and limbs. Qatada said: He is a witness against himself. In another narration he said: If you wish, by God you will see him seeing the faults and sins of people, yet heedless of his own. And it was said: It is written in the Gospel: O son of Adam, you see the speck in your brother’s eye and leave the log in your own eye and do not see it! Ibn Zayd, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said the same, and Ibn Jarir preferred it. Qatadah said on the authority of Zurarah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Even if he presents his excuses means: If he throws down his clothes. Ad-Dahhak said: Even if he throws down his curtain. Have you not heard that He said: Their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers and that He said: “And they will offer to God that Day peace” {So they will offer peace: We had not done any evil} and their statement: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists}.

What he said is similar to the statement of God the Almighty: {Their glances will not return to them}, meaning they will look in terror like this and that, their sight not settling on anything due to the intensity of the terror. Others read it with a fatha, which is close in meaning to the first. It is said: It refers to disbelief in the truth before the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: To explode before him means to go ahead riding his head. Al-Hasan said: No son of Adam will be encountered except that his soul is drawn to disobeying God step by step, except for the one whom God protects. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and more than one of the early Muslims: He is the one who hastens to commit sins and delays repentance. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is the disbeliever who denies the Day of Reckoning. Ibn Zayd said the same, and this is what is most apparent of what is meant. That is why He said after it: He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?' That is, he says, When will the Day of Resurrection be? His question is a question of improbability of its occurrence and a denial of its existence, as God the Almighty said: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you should be truthful?' Say, 'You have an appointment for a Day from which you will not delay an hour, nor will you advance it.' And God the Almighty said here: {And when the sight is dazed} Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ read it with a kasra on the ra’, meaning dazzled. What he said is similar to the statement of God the Almighty: {Their glances will not return to them}, meaning they will look in terror like this and that, their sight not settling on anything due to the intensity of the terror. Others read it with a fatha, which is close in meaning to the first. The point is that the eyes will be dazzled on the Day of Resurrection and will be humbled, bewildered, and humiliated by the intensity of the horrors and the enormity of what they will witness on the Day of Resurrection of matters. And the statement of God the Almighty: {And the moon will be eclipsed}, meaning its light will be gone. And the sun and the moon will be joined together Mujahid said: coiled. Ibn Zayd read when explaining this verse: {When the sun is wrapped up * And when the stars are extinguished}. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read: And the sun and the moon will be joined together. That is, is there a refuge or a place of refuge? God the Almighty says: No! No burden! To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and more than one of the early Muslims said: That is, there is no escape. This verse is like God the Almighty’s saying: For you there is no refuge that Day, nor will you be denied. That is, you will have no place to flee in. Likewise, He said here: No burden, that is, you will have no place to seek refuge in. That is why He said: To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement, that is, the return and destination. Then God the Almighty said: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind meaning he will be informed of all his deeds, old and new, first and last, small and great, as God the Almighty said: “And they will find present what they did. And your Lord does not wrong anyone” and likewise He said here: Rather, man is a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses meaning he is a witness against himself and knows what he did, even if he apologizes and denies it. And as God the Almighty said: “Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant.” And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rather, man is a witness against himself meaning: his hearing, sight, hands, feet and limbs. Qatada said: He is a witness against himself. In another narration he said: If you wish, by God you will see him seeing the faults and sins of people, yet heedless of his own. 75:16: This is an instruction from God the Almighty to His Messenger (peace be upon him) on how to receive revelation from the angel. He would hasten to receive it and race the angel in reciting it. God the Almighty commanded him when the angel came to him with revelation to listen to it and God guaranteed to gather it in his chest and make it easy for him to recite it in the manner in which it was revealed to him, and to explain it to him, interpret it and clarify it. The first case is gathering it in his chest, the second is reciting it, and the third is interpreting it and clarifying its meaning. That is why God Almighty said: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it meaning the Qur’an, as God Almighty said: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you and say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge’ Then God Almighty said: Indeed, upon Us is its collection meaning in your chest and its recitation meaning that you recite it. So when We have recited it meaning when the angel recites it to you on behalf of God Almighty: then follow its recitation meaning listen to it and then recite it as it was recited to you. Then upon Us is its clarification meaning after memorizing it and reciting it, We will explain it to you and clarify it and inspire you with its meaning according to what We intended and prescribed. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman narrated to us from Abu Uwanah from Musa ibn Abi Aisha from Saeed ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was struggling with the severity of the revelation and he would move his lips.” Ibn Abbas said to me: “I move my lips as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) moved his lips.” Saeed said to me: And I move my lips as I saw Ibn Abbas move his lips. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” He said: “Collect it in your chest and then you recite it. ‘So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.’” That is, listen to it and be silent. Then upon Us is its clarification. So after that, whenever Gabriel departed, he would recite it as I had recited it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it through other chains of narration on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha. The wording of Al-Bukhari is: When Gabriel came to him, he would lower his head, and when he left, he would recite it as God, the Almighty, had promised him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Yahya Al-Taimi narrated to us, Musa bin Abi Aisha narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Whenever revelation was sent down to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he would encounter difficulty from it. Whenever it was sent down to him, he would be known to move his lips, receiving the beginning and moving his lips with it, lest he forget the beginning before he finished the end.” So God, the Most High, revealed: Move not your tongue with it, to hasten it. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Mujahid, Al-Dahhak and others said: This verse was revealed about that. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas: Move not your tongue with it, to hasten it. He said: He would not stop reciting for fear that he would forget it, so God, the Most High, said: “Move not your tongue with it, to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection” means to collect it for you and its recitation means to recite it to you so that you do not forget. Ibn Abbas and Atiyyah Al-Awfi said: Then upon Us is its clarification means to clarify what is lawful and unlawful. Qatadah also said this. God the Almighty says: {No! Rather, you love that immediate life and neglect the Hereafter.} meaning, what drives them to deny the Day of Resurrection and to disobey what God the Almighty revealed to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of the true revelation and the Noble Qur’an is that their only concern is this immediate worldly life, and they are heedless and distracted from the Hereafter. Then God the Almighty says: {Some faces, that Day, will be radiant.} From radiance, meaning beautiful, bright, radiant, and joyful. {Looking at their Lord.} That is, seeing Him with their own eyes, as Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him narrated in his Sahih: {Indeed, you will see your Lord with your own eyes.} It has been proven that the believers will see God Almighty in the Hereafter in the authentic hadiths through continuous chains of transmission among the scholars of hadith, which cannot be denied or prohibited. This is due to the hadith of Abu Sa`id and Abu Hurayrah, both of which are in the two Sahihs, in which some people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Do you find it difficult to see the sun and the moon when there are no clouds in front of them? They said: No. He said: Then you will see your Lord like that. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon! So if you can avoid being overcome in prayer before sunrise or before sunset, then do so. Rather, you love that immediate life and neglect the Hereafter.} meaning, what drives them to deny the Day of Resurrection and to disobey what God the Almighty revealed to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of the true revelation and the Noble Qur’an is that their only concern is this immediate worldly life, and they are heedless and distracted from the Hereafter. Then God the Almighty says: {Some faces, that Day, will be radiant.} From radiance, meaning beautiful, bright, radiant, and joyful. {Looking at their Lord.} That is, seeing Him with their own eyes, as Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him narrated in his Sahih: {Indeed, you will see your Lord with your own eyes.} It has been proven that the believers will see God Almighty in the Hereafter in the authentic hadiths through continuous chains of transmission among the scholars of hadith, which cannot be denied or prohibited. This is due to the hadith of Abu Sa`id and Abu Hurayrah, both of which are in the two Sahihs, in which some people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Do you find it difficult to see the sun and the moon when there are no clouds in front of them? They said: No. He said: Then you will see your Lord like that. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon! So if you can avoid being overcome in prayer before sunrise or before sunset, then do so. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them. They will say: Did You not make our faces white? Did You not admit us to Paradise and save us from the Fire? He will say: Then the veil will be lifted, and they will not be given anything more beloved to them than looking at their Lord, which is the increase.” Then he recited this verse: For those who do good is the best and more. He said: And it was narrated by Abd al-Malik ibn Abhar, on the authority of Nuwayr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar. And likewise it was narrated by al-Thawri, on the authority of Nuwayr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he did not trace it back to the Prophet. Were it not for the fear of making it too long, we would have included the hadiths with their chains of transmission and wordings from the Sahihs, Hasan, Musnads, and Sunans, but we mentioned that in separate places in this commentary. And success is from God. This, praise be to God, is agreed upon by the Companions, the Followers, and the early generations of this nation, as it is agreed upon by the Imams of Islam and the guides of mankind. Whoever interprets this to mean that what is meant by to is the singular of blessings, which are blessings, as al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, Looking to her Lord, he said: Waiting for the reward from her Lord. Ibn Jarir narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Mujahid, and Abu Salih also said the same. This speaker has gone far astray and has invalidated what he has gone to, and where is he in relation to the words of God Almighty: No indeed! They will be veiled from their Lord, that Day. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: The disbelievers were not veiled except when it was known that the righteous will see Him, the Almighty and Majestic. Then there are many reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicating what the context of the noble verse indicates, which is His words, the Almighty: Looking to her Lord, Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari told us, Adam told us, al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, Hasana said: Looking to her Lord, he said: Looking to the Creator, and it is right for her to be radiant, and she is looking to…” The Creator. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And some faces, that Day, will be gloomy, thinking that some terrible disaster will befall them} These are the faces of the wicked that will be gloomy on the Day of Resurrection. Qatada said: Gloomy. As-Suddi said: Their colors will change. Ibn Zayd said: Gloomy means scowling. Thinking means certain that some terrible disaster will befall them. Mujahid said: A disaster. Qatada said: Evil. As-Suddi said: Certain that they will perish. Ibn Zayd said: Thinking that they will enter the Fire. This situation is similar to the saying of God the Almighty: {The Day some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black} and the saying of God the Almighty: {Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, laughing and rejoicing. And some faces, that Day, will be covered with dust. Darkness will cover them. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked} and the saying of God the Almighty: {Some faces, that Day, will be humbly submissive, toiling, burning in a blazing Fire} until His saying: {Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, well-pleased with their striving, in a lofty Garden} in similar verses and contexts.
75:26: The Almighty tells us about the state of death and the horrors that await us there. God has established us there with the firm statement, so the Almighty said: No! When it reaches the collarbones. If we make No! a deterrent, then its meaning is that you, O son of Adam, will not be lying there about what you have been told, but rather it has become evident to you. And if we make it mean truly, then it is apparent, meaning truly, when it reaches the collarbones, that is, your soul has been extracted from your body and reached your collarbones. The collarbone is the plural of collarbone, which are the bones between the opening in the throat and the shoulder, like the Almighty’s saying: “Then why, when it reaches the throat, * And you are at that time looking on, * And We are nearer to it than you, but you do not see, * Then why, if you are not to be held accountable, * Do you not return it, if you should be truthful?” And thus He said here: No! When it reaches the collarbones. And here he mentions the hadith of Bishr bin Hajjaj that was mentioned earlier in Surat Yasin. The clavicle is the plural of collarbone and it is close to the throat. “And it was said: from the one who recites” Akrima said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning from the one who recites, he is recited. Abu Qilabah said the same. And it was said from the one who recites meaning from a doctor who heals. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Nasr ibn Ali told us, Rawh ibn Al-Musayyab Abu Raja Al-Kalbi told us, Amr ibn Malik told us on the authority of Abu Al-Juza’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And it was said from the one who recites It was said: Who recites with his soul, the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment? Based on this, it is from the speech of the angels. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, he said: The world and the Hereafter shall be entwined for him. And this is what Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, meaning the last day of the worldly life will be the first day of the Hereafter, so hardship will meet hardship except for whom God has mercy. And Ikrimah said: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, meaning a great matter with a great matter. And Mujahid said: One affliction with another. And Al-Hasan Al-Basri said regarding the statement of God, the Most High, And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, they are your two legs if they are entwined. And in a narration on his authority, his legs died and could not carry him, although he was carried on them. And this is what Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik, and in a narration on Al-Hasan: He wrapped them in the shroud. And Ad-Dahhak said: And the leg shall be entwined with the leg, two matters came together for him: the people prepared his body and the angels prepared his soul. God the Almighty says: To your Lord, that Day, is the return, meaning the place of return and destination. This is because the soul is raised to the heavens, and God the Almighty says: Return My servant to the earth, for from it I created them, and into it I will return them, and from it I will extract them another time, as mentioned in the long hadith of Al-Bara’. God the Almighty also said: “And He is the Prevailing over His servants. And He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail [in their duties]. Then they will be returned to God, their Master, the Truth. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.” And the saying of God, the Most High: He neither believed nor prayed, * But he lied and turned away. This is a description of the disbeliever who was in this worldly abode denying the truth in his heart and turning away from working with his body, so there is no good in him inwardly or outwardly. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: “He neither believed nor prayed, * But he lied and turned away. * Then he went to his family, swaggering.” That is, rejoicing, vain, arrogant, lazy, with no ambition or work, as God, the Most High, said: And when they return to their families, they return in joy. And God, the Most High, said: “Indeed, he was among his family, rejoicing. Indeed, he thought that he would never return.” That is, Yes, indeed his Lord was ever, seeing of him. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then he went to his family, swaggering. Qatadah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: Swaggering. God the Almighty said: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting. This is a clear threat and warning from God the Almighty to the disbeliever who walks arrogantly, meaning that you have the right to walk like this, even though you have disbelieved in your Creator and Maker, as is said in such a case by way of mockery and threat, like His the Almighty’s saying: “Taste. Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble.” And His the Almighty’s saying: “Eat and enjoy yourselves a little. Indeed, you are criminals.” And His the Almighty’s saying: Then worship whatever you will besides Him. And His the Almighty’s saying: Do whatever you will, and so on. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha, who said: I asked Sa’id ibn Jubayr, It is more fitting for you, then more fitting, then more fitting. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said this to Abu Jahl, and then the Qur’an was revealed regarding it. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us H and Abu Dawud narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us on the authority of Musa ibn Abi 'Aisha on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it to Abu Jahl and then God the Almighty revealed it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us on the authority of Ishaq, Sa'id narrated to us on the authority of Qatadah, regarding his statement: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, is a warning following a warning as you hear. They claimed that the enemy of God, Abu Jahl, grabbed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by the hem of his garment and then said: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you. The enemy of God, Abu Jahl, said: Are you threatening me, O Muhammad? By God, neither you nor your Lord can do anything, and I am more powerful than one who walks between two mountains. God the Almighty says: {Does man think that he will be left neglected?} As-Suddi said: It means that he will not be resurrected. Mujahid, Ash-Shafi’i and Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It means that he will not be commanded or forbidden. It appears that the verse includes both situations, i.e. he will not be left neglected in this world, neither commanded nor forbidden, nor will he be left neglected in his grave, not resurrected. Rather, he will be commanded and forbidden in this world, and will be gathered to God in the Hereafter. The purpose here is to prove the Resurrection and refute those who deny it from the people of misguidance, ignorance and stubbornness. For this reason, God the Almighty said, proving the Resurrection by the Beginning, {Was he not a drop of emitted semen?} i.e., was not man a weak drop of despised water. Emitted means that which is emitted from the loins into the wombs. Then he was a clot, then He created and proportioned meaning, he became a clot, then a lump of flesh, then He took form and breathed into him the soul, so he became a sound creation with sound limbs, male or female, by God’s permission and decree. For this reason God the Almighty said: Then He made from him the two mates, the male and the female Al-Rum 13:1-14. Then He the Almighty said: Is not He able to give life to the dead? Meaning, is He not the One who created this sound creation from this weak sperm able to restore it as He began it? The ability to restore is either by way of priority in relation to the beginning or by equality, according to the two opinions in God the Almighty’s statement: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him Al-Rum 13:1-14. The first is more well-known, as was explained and confirmed in Surat Al-Rum, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Shababah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Musa bin Abi A’ishah, on the authority of another person, that he was on a roof reading the Qur’an and raising his voice. When he recited, Is He not able to give life to the dead? he said, Glory be to You, O God. So, yes. He was asked about that and he said, “I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say that.” Abu Dawud, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi A’ishah, who said, A man was praying on the roof of his house, and when he recited, “Is He not able to give life to the dead? he said, Glory be to You. So, yes. He was asked about that and he said, “I heard it from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.” Abu Dawud is the only one who narrated it, and he did not name this companion, but that does not matter.” Abu Dawud also said: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us, Sufyan told us, Ismail bin Umayya told me, I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among you recites ‘By the Fig and the Olive’ and reaches the end of it, ‘Is not God the best of judges?’ let him say, ‘Yes, and I am of that among the witnesses. And whoever recites, ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection,’ and reaches the words, ‘Is He not able to give life to the dead?’ let him say, ‘Yes.’ And whoever recites, ‘By the Messengers,’ and reaches, ‘Then in what statement after it will they believe?’ let him say, ‘We believe in God.’” Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Umar, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah with it. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, who said: I said to him, ‘Who narrated it to you?’ He said: A truthful man on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: Is He not able to give life to the dead? He mentioned to us that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, he would say: Glory be to You, and yes indeed. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he passed by this verse: Is He not able to give life to the dead? He said: Glory be to You, and yes indeed. The end of the interpretation of Surat al-Qiyamah. All praise and thanks are due to God.

He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said this to Abu Jahl, and then the Qur’an was revealed regarding it. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us H and Abu Dawud narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us on the authority of Musa ibn Abi 'Aisha on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it to Abu Jahl and then God the Almighty revealed it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us on the authority of Ishaq, Sa'id narrated to us on the authority of Qatadah, regarding his statement: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, is a warning following a warning as you hear. They claimed that the enemy of God, Abu Jahl, grabbed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by the hem of his garment and then said: That which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you, then that which is more fitting for you. The enemy of God, Abu Jahl, said: Are you threatening me, O Muhammad? By God, neither you nor your Lord can do anything, and I am more powerful than one who walks between two mountains. God the Almighty says: {Does man think that he will be left neglected?} As-Suddi said: It means that he will not be resurrected. Mujahid, Ash-Shafi’i and Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It means that he will not be commanded or forbidden. It appears that the verse includes both situations, i.e. he will not be left neglected in this world, neither commanded nor forbidden, nor will he be left neglected in his grave, not resurrected. Rather, he will be commanded and forbidden in this world, and will be gathered to God in the Hereafter. The purpose here is to prove the Resurrection and refute those who deny it from the people of misguidance, ignorance and stubbornness. For this reason, God the Almighty said, proving the Resurrection by the Beginning, {Was he not a drop of emitted semen?} i.e., was not man a weak drop of despised water. Emitted means that which is emitted from the loins into the wombs. Then he was a clot, then He created and proportioned meaning, he became a clot, then a lump of flesh, then He took form and breathed into him the soul, so he became a sound creation with sound limbs, male or female, by God’s permission and decree. For this reason God the Almighty said: Then He made from him the two mates, the male and the female Al-Rum 13:1-14. Then He the Almighty said: Is not He able to give life to the dead? Meaning, is He not the One who created this sound creation from this weak sperm able to restore it as He began it? The ability to restore is either by way of priority in relation to the beginning or by equality, according to the two opinions in God the Almighty’s statement: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him Al-Rum 13:1-14. The first is more well-known, as was explained and confirmed in Surat Al-Rum, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Shababah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Musa bin Abi A’ishah, on the authority of another person, that he was on a roof reading the Qur’an and raising his voice. When he recited, Is He not able to give life to the dead? he said, Glory be to You, O God. So, yes. He was asked about that and he said, “I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say that.” Abu Dawud, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi A’ishah, who said, A man was praying on the roof of his house, and when he recited, “Is He not able to give life to the dead? he said, Glory be to You. So, yes. He was asked about that and he said, “I heard it from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.” Abu Dawud is the only one who narrated it, and he did not name this companion, but that does not matter.” Abu Dawud also said: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us, Sufyan told us, Ismail bin Umayya told me, I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among you recites ‘By the Fig and the Olive’ and reaches the end of it, ‘Is not God the best of judges?’ let him say, ‘Yes, and I am of that among the witnesses. And whoever recites, ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection,’ and reaches the words, ‘Is He not able to give life to the dead?’ let him say, ‘Yes.’ And whoever recites, ‘By the Messengers,’ and reaches, ‘Then in what statement after it will they believe?’ let him say, ‘We believe in God.’” Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Umar, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah with it. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, who said: I said to him, ‘Who narrated it to you?’ He said: A truthful man on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: Is He not able to give life to the dead? He mentioned to us that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, he would say: Glory be to You, and yes indeed. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he passed by this verse: Is He not able to give life to the dead? He said: Glory be to You, and yes indeed. The end of the interpretation of Surat al-Qiyamah. All praise and thanks are due to God.
